page: Vultr vhf-16c-58gb is an instance within the High Frequency Compute family. The server provides 16 vCPUs derived from 8 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz with hyperthreading enabled under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 58.0 GB of system memory, which yields approximately 3.62 GB of RAM per vCPU, and incorporates 1024 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, and no discrete graphics processing hardware is present.

The CPU architecture supports standard instruction extensions including AVX, AES-NI, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are unavailable. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance displays average processing capacity, recording a stress-ng multi-core metric of 14058.95 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6764.0. In software compilation tests using Clang, it reaches a score of 14012.0, while PassMark physics performance falls within the lower quartile at 731.79.

Memory and input/output benchmarks illustrate distinct throughput characteristics. Small-block cached read memory bandwidth operates at 907.89 GB/sec. In contrast, large-block uncached memory operations register in the lower tiers, achieving 24.85 GB/sec read and 13.66 GB/sec write bandwidth. The integrated 1024 GB NVMe drive supports localized data access, enabling Redis SET operations of 11.03 million operations per second and standard database workloads, though static web serving capacity is comparatively lower at 6.08 GB/sec.

Given its balanced ratio of memory to compute combined with integrated high-capacity NVMe storage, vhf-16c-58gb offers solid density for software development pipelines, compilation environments, caching services, and relational database hosting that do not continuously saturate uncached memory channels.
description: Vultr vhf-16c-58gb is an x86_64 compute instance featuring 16 shared vCPUs mapped across 8 physical Intel cores running at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 58.0 GB of memory and 1024 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. It provides a balanced ratio of 3.62 GB of RAM per vCPU without discrete GPU acceleration. Benchmark measurements show median-tier execution across general compute metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6764.0, a Clang compilation score of 14012.0, and Redis SET throughput of 11.03 million operations per second. However, uncached memory bandwidth is constrained, measuring 24.85 GB/sec for reads and 13.66 GB/sec for writes. The included high-capacity NVMe drive provides direct storage access, positioning this server for general-purpose web applications, continuous integration pipelines, development environments, and relational or caching database systems that do not saturate uncached memory buses.
